To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prenatal dexamethazone therapy in premature children is associated with a lower incidence of neurological complications in the first year of life.
prenatal dexamethsone therapy is associated with a lower incidence of severe cerebral palsy and a higher incidence of minor developmental delay in premature children at the age of 24–36 months.
prenatal treatment with dexamethasome is associated with a lower incidence of neurological complications in preterm children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the detection of the effect of the prenatal dexamethasonetreated and in 22% of the placebo group.
the study of the role of the immune system and of the cytokines in the pathogenesis of the preterm labour and the development of the neonatal lung disease.
the development of an integrated approach to the study of human behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

prenatal dexamethasonetreatment is associated with a lower incidence of neonatal neurological complications, but the effect on the long‐term neurological development of premature children is less obvious and requires further investigation.
the use of prenatal steroids in preterm children may have a beneficial effect on neurological development, but the results of our follow‐up study should be confirmed in larger randomized studies.
the beneficial effects of antenatal glucocorticoid therapy on neonatal outcome are not necessarily accompanied by an improvement in long‐term neurological and developmental outcome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of prenatal glucocorticoide treatment is justified in order to prevent neonatal complications in premature children.

the beneficial effect on the neonatal course is followed by a lower frequency of cerebral palsy at the age of two years, but not by a lower incidence or severity of minor neurological or developmental delay.

the beneficial effects of prenatal glucocorticoide treatment on the incidence of cerebral complications (intraventricular haematoma or periventriculae leukomalacia) during the neonatal course are followed by a lower rate of cerebral palsy at the age of two years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benefits of prenatal glucocortocoid treatment may persist into childhood and adolescence.
prenatal steroids may have a positive effect on the long‐term neurodevelopment of preterm children.
prenatal dexamethasonetreatment does not affect the neurological development at 24 months of age.
